A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods, experiments, and Appendices A–C. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GCN-oracle comparisons and hallucination-detection experiments, including AUROC/AURAC results and computational-cost comparisons in Figures 2–9 and Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an Appendix C.2 example containing sampled target/verifier responses and their consistency scores.

M1.justification: The GCN formulation, weighted MPD combination, and two-stage thresholding procedure in Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The symmetrized kernel introduced in the geometric discussion does not establish a change to the implemented detection procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate QA hallucination detection on SQuAD, TriviaQA, and Natural Questions. The added song-question example remains within this task coverage; summarization and long-form generation are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SE, MPD, EigV, Ecc, KLE, and the GCN-based oracle. The target and verifier models in the new example already participate in the existing experiments.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same models, temperatures of 0.1 and 1.0, ten sampled answers, GPT-4 judging, AUROC/AURAC metrics, and 400-example validation/test sets under the same two validation scenarios. New footnotes justify existing choices without revising them.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds one case study illustrating complementary information from a weaker verifier: Llama-3-70B-Instruct repeatedly names Elkie Brooks, while Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 identifies the supplied correct answer, Chris Rea. Existing sensitivity and threshold-transfer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds, averages, and standard deviations, with unchanged uncertainty displays. The newly quoted human/GPT-4 agreement percentages are attributed to prior work, not new statistical evaluation of this paper.

E6.justification: The benchmark plots and Table 1 retain their results, including p(95) values of 86.5, 78.5, and 72.0. Appendix C.2 newly reports self-consistency MPD of 0.183 and cross-model MPD of 0.922 for the added example, alongside the sampled responses.

T1.justification: Section 5 changes the reproducing-kernel assumption from the entailment kernel E to a symmetrized kernel E′. A new footnote specifies bidirectional averaging and states MPD invariance under symmetrization. Theorem 5.1 and the proofs and derivations in Appendices A–B remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly qualifies the experimental evidence as QA-style detection. The conclusion newly asserts that the framework is task-agnostic and anticipates similar effects beyond QA where semantic equivalence is assessable. The main saturation, verifier-benefit, and computational-saving claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains the QA restriction through the difficulty of evaluating long, open-ended outputs and explicitly identifies validation-set dependence as a limitation. It also adds literature-based rationales for ten samples and GPT-4 labeling, without new experiments validating those choices.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly discloses that experiments used eight RTX A6000 GPUs. Section 4.1 also aligns its entailment-estimator example with deberta-v2-xlarge-mnli, which Section 6 already specified in v1; this does not establish an experimental model change.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive positioning relative to self-consistency methods, SAC3, confidence elicitation, and hallucination mitigation remain unchanged. Additional references to already cited works support explanations of experimental choices.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, opening paragraph, selected explanations, and captions; adds explanatory paragraphs and footnotes; and renames Section 7 to Conclusion and Discussion. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Document-wide reformatting replaces the ICML-style presentation with TMLR typography, front matter, spacing, and figure placement. Figures 1 and 5 use side captions, Algorithm 1 is compacted, and Figure 6 changes label styling and tick presentation. The existing figures and results table are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 more clearly states the empirical scope and validation-set limitation, refines the kernel assumption, discloses hardware, and illustrates verifier complementarity with a concrete example. These modestly improve transparency and interpretation. Quantitative benchmark evidence and proofs are unchanged, and the new expectation of applicability beyond QA remains untested.
